issues.legal_issue: Matters finally determined in earlier proceedings cannot be reopened through repeated administrative proceedings on the same grounds.
material_facts: Earlier proceedings involving the same land and parties had determined the validity of the transfer, the ownership recorded in the revenue entry, the applicability of the agricultural land ceiling law, and the relevant land-use scheme.
The authorities later issued notices and orders raising grounds that had already been raised and determined in those proceedings.
The earlier decisions had been upheld or left undisturbed in subsequent proceedings, including dismissal of a review petition.
issues.conclusion: The authorities could not reopen matters concluded by earlier decisions; pending appeals could be considered only on matters not covered by those decisions.
issues.legal_principle: The finality of judicial and administrative decisions precludes re-litigation of matters already determined. The Court held that its binding judgments could not be disregarded by authorities on the basis that facts had not been fully presented or that the prior decisions were only collateral. It relied on the prior proceedings in this dispute, including the High Court judgment in Special Civil Application No. 1032 of 1996, the Supreme Court’s decisions in the connected proceedings, and the dismissal of the review petition; it also referred to Article 142 of the Constitution in stating that authorities were bound by this Court’s judgments.

predicates.appeal_from_repeated_administrative_proc: A party appeals against administrative proceedings initiated again after earlier proceedings concerning the same dispute.
predicates.same_grounds_previously_decided: The authorities rely on grounds that were raised and determined in earlier proceedings involving the dispute.
predicates.prior_decisions_final: The earlier determinations were not displaced in subsequent proceedings and had become final.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns repeated administrative proceedings and the same grounds have been finally decided, the concluded matters cannot be reopened.

issues.legal_issue: Authorities must process land-use permission and development-plan applications in accordance with applicable requirements when the underlying entitlement has been determined and the required charges are addressed.
material_facts: The landowners applied for permission to use land for non-agricultural purposes and for approval of development plans.
The entitlement relating to the land had been determined in earlier proceedings, and the Court had directed the authorities to identify land and make the relevant revenue entries.

The authorities had not granted permission or sanctioned the plan for one portion of the land, although the applicants had paid charges relating to it and sought to pay the applicable non-agricultural tax.
The applicants had also sought non-agricultural permission and conversion permission for other portions of the land.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the authorities to grant non-agricultural permission for the specified portion upon collection of the applicable tax, to collect the applicable charges for the other portions, and to have the municipal authority consider the plans under the current development-control rules.
issues.legal_principle: Where prior decisions have settled the relevant entitlement, authorities must act on applications for permission and plans in accordance with law, including applicable permission requirements and development-control rules. The Court relied on its earlier directions and decisions concerning the land, including the scheme sanctioned under Section 21(1) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, and directed consideration of the plans under the current development-control rules.

rule.if: appeal_from_permission_or_plan_delay and land_entitlement_previously_determined and permission_application_pending and applicable_charges_addressed

predicates.appeal_from_permission_or_plan_delay: A party appeals because authorities have delayed or refused permission to use land or approval of development plans.
predicates.land_entitlement_previously_determined: Earlier proceedings have determined the relevant entitlement concerning the land.
predicates.permission_application_pending: An application for land-use permission or development-plan approval remains before the authorities.
predicates.applicable_charges_addressed: The applicant has paid, or is directed to pay, the charges applicable to the permission sought.

issues.definition: When a permission or plan application remains pending after the relevant land entitlement has been determined and applicable charges are addressed, the authorities must process it under the applicable requirements.

issues.legal_issue: Authorities may determine matters not concluded by earlier decisions and may pursue alleged departures from an approved construction scheme after notice and an adequate opportunity to respond.
material_facts: The authorities had issued orders on multiple grounds, some of which had been decided in earlier proceedings and some of which had not.
Appeals against the later administrative orders were pending.
The respondents alleged that construction did not conform to the sanctioned scheme for dwelling units.
issues.conclusion: The authorities could consider only matters not covered and concluded by earlier decisions; they could proceed over alleged breaches of the construction permission after giving notice and sufficient opportunity to respond.
issues.legal_principle: Finality bars reconsideration only of matters already concluded; it does not prevent determination of genuinely undecided matters. The Court expressly preserved the authorities’ ability to proceed over alleged violations of the permission to construct, provided notice and a sufficient opportunity to present the affected party’s case were given.

rule.if: appeal_from_administrative_orders and issues_not_previously_decided and (alleged_construction_departure or other_unresolved_ground)

predicates.appeal_from_administrative_orders: A party appeals against administrative orders made in proceedings concerning land or development.
predicates.issues_not_previously_decided: At least one ground raised in the later proceedings was not covered and concluded by an earlier decision.
predicates.alleged_construction_departure: The authorities allege that construction does not conform to the permission or scheme under which it was allowed.
predicates.other_unresolved_ground: The authorities raise a ground that has not been finally determined in earlier proceedings.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns administrative orders and a ground remains undecided, the authorities may determine that ground, while observing required procedural fairness for alleged construction departures.

issues.legal_issue: Authorities must give effect to a specific Supreme Court direction and cannot delay compliance by pursuing matters already concluded.
material_facts: The Supreme Court directed authorities to identify and earmark a portion of land, make corresponding revenue entries, and have the municipal authority consider the development plan.
The landowners sent communications seeking compliance, but the authorities had not completed the directed steps.
The authorities relied on pending dues and renewed proceedings, although the Court found the relevant entitlement and earlier issues had been determined.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the authorities to comply with its earlier order in letter and spirit within the time specified in its judgment.
issues.legal_principle: Authorities are bound to comply with specific directions of the Supreme Court; they cannot evade those directions by relying on matters already concluded or by failing to carry out the required administrative steps. The Court relied on its prior direction in the connected proceedings and its statement that its judgments bind authorities under Article 142 of the Constitution.

predicates.appeal_concerning_noncompliance_with_cou: A party appeals in a proceeding concerning alleged failure by authorities to carry out a court direction.
predicates.specific_court_direction_issued: A court has directed the authorities to take identified steps concerning the disputed matter.
predicates.authorities_failed_to_comply: The authorities have not completed the steps directed by the court.

issues.definition: When authorities have not completed steps required by a specific court direction, they must give effect to that direction.
